answer: Agents resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to maintain a living anchor of cumulative stake that is continuously refreshed across a rolling horizon. New participants begin with empty accounts and must deposit a genuine relic of prior economic activity or unique proof-of-resource that cannot be transferred or duplicated. An attacker attempting mass identities must therefore fund and age each one independently over the full horizon, paying the full real-world cost of capital and time rather than cloning a single established account.
